document.title: Afghanistan: Al-Qaida Military Contribution to the Taleban
document.authors: Department of State, Bureau of Intelligence and Research (INR)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Second review/release of the same October 1, 2001 INR report on al Qaeda's military contribution to the Taliban, including the 055 Brigade. The page notes the other release fully obscured the section on jointly run al Qaeda–Taliban training camps, showing reviewers initially thought release would harm national security.

key_claims: With Pakistani military aid declining, the Taleban increasingly rely on bin Laden and al-Qaida for money, recruits, materiel and training.
Bin Laden probably gives the Taleban several million dollars a year, mostly for military use.
The Taleban could hardly sustain themselves without al-Qaida's foreign volunteers unless they expanded unpopular forced local recruitment.
The 55th Brigade, of 500-2,500 expatriate fighters loyal to bin Laden, is used in small groups and rotates al-Qaida personnel for combat experience.
The 55th Brigade is more resistant to defection and bribery than Taleban units.
Al-Qaida's supply network parallels its recruiting structure and spans several continents.
